rationale: C03 plausibly supplied a material template. Both memoranda reject narrowly targeted relief because the beneficiary or beneficiaries have not justified special treatment under generally applicable rules, then emphasize that approval would establish an undesirable precedent encouraging comparable claims by others. The progression from facts, to lack of justification for exceptional treatment, to precedent-based disapproval is unusually close, and C03 was issued only six days before the child. C20 and C06 share similar general-law-versus-private-relief reasoning, but their drafting structures and language are less closely aligned.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Justification for such unusual treatment has not been shown.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The bill would give special treatment to a single community and thereby discriminate against other communities
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the proposed private relief as unjustified exceptional treatment relative to similarly situated parties.

shared_material.child_excerpt: To approve S. 3941 would, I believe, establish an undesirable precedent, encouraging others to seek relief from laws of general applicability on expired mining claims.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The bill would set a precedent which could be used by many other communities to urge cancellation of their obligations held by the Federal Government.
shared_material.explanation: The central closing rationale is materially parallel: approving one exception would encourage many analogous requests for relief from generally applicable obligations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Under the circumstances, I have no recourse but to withhold my approval of S. 3941.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This bill involves one community and a relatively small amount of money; but it would establish undesirable principles and precedents affecting many other communities and many millions of dollars. I have, therefore, withheld my approval of S. 2182.
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude by linking the precedent concern directly to withholding approval.
